airplane: Characterized by a distinct elongated fuselage and wings shape, airplanes are individual aircraft parked on concrete aprons or along taxiways, contrasting with the long paved strips of runways, the vast multi-building complexes of airports, or the scattered machinery of industrial areas.
airport: Identified by a large complex of multiple terminal buildings, hangars, and interconnected taxiways surrounding long paved strips, unlike isolated runways, individual parked airplanes, or railway stations which focus on linear tracks and passenger platforms.
baseball_diamond: Features a distinct square diamond shape with an infield dirt texture and outfield grass, distinguishing it from the continuous greens and sand traps of golf courses, the massive oval structures of stadiums, or the clustered rectangular roofs of mobile home parks.
basketball_court: Displays a rectangular paved surface with distinct backboard circles and court lines, unlike the smaller nets and continuous sidelines of tennis courts, the unordered grid of parked vehicles in parking lots, or the surrounding houses and trees of medium residential areas.
beach: Shows a distinct narrow border of bright sandy or pebbly texture directly adjacent to water bodies and land, unlike the fully surrounded landmasses of islands, the vast inland expanses of deserts, or the docked boats and piers of harbors.
bridge: Characterized by a linear structure spanning across a water body or deep valley with distinct support pillars, differing from overpasses that cross roads or railways, the water-bound docks of harbors, or the continuous flat asphalt of freeways.
chaparral: Exhibits a sparse, scrubby vegetation texture with patches of bare earth, contrasting with the barren sand of deserts, the steep rocky elevations of mountains, or the dense continuous canopy of forests.
church: Identified by a main building featuring a prominent steeple or cross-shaped layout, often surrounded by a parking lot, setting it apart from the sprawling symmetrical wings of palaces, the dense grid of smaller homes in medium residential areas, or the high-rise buildings of commercial areas.
circular_farmland: Characterized by large circular green or brown agricultural patches with central pivot irrigation, unlike the straight-edged plots of rectangular farmlands, the small metallic domes of storage tanks, or the irregular water-soaked terrains of wetlands.
cloud: Displays a soft, fluffy, and amorphous white texture drifting over terrestrial or aquatic surfaces, distinguishing it from the permanent bright white peaks attached to mountains, the geometric cooling towers of thermal power stations, or the flat stationary blue water of lakes.
commercial_area: Features a dense cluster of large rectangular commercial buildings with surrounding parking grids, unlike the warehouses and smokestacks of industrial areas, the ornate historical architecture of palaces, or the open paved lots of parking areas.
dense_residential: Characterized by tightly packed small buildings with very little vegetation or space between them, unlike the more spacious yards of medium residential areas, the uniform narrow rectangles of mobile home parks, or the large commercial structures of business districts.
desert: Shows vast expanses of uniform sandy or rocky texture with no vegetation, unlike the sparse scrubby plants of chaparral, the steep elevated topography of mountains, or the narrow coastal strips of beaches.
forest: Identified by a continuous, dense canopy of tree coverage with a rough, textured surface, contrasting with the geometric crop lines of rectangular farmlands, the mixed water and marshy textures of wetlands, or the clustered rectangular roofs of mobile home parks.
freeway: Characterized by long, continuous, multi-lane paved roads with smooth curves and connecting ramps, lacking the tiered structure of overpasses, the immense width and center lines of runways, or the crossing junctions of intersections.
golf_course: Displays a vast expanse of manicured green grass with irregular curving sand traps and small water hazards, unlike the small diamond shape of baseball fields, the long paved strips of runways, or the dense unmanaged canopy of forests.
ground_track_field: Features an oval or rectangular track surrounding a central green infield, distinguishing it from the massive enclosing seating structures of stadiums, the diamond layout of baseball fields, or the small rectangles of tennis courts.
harbor: Identified by a coastal area with multiple docked vessels, linear piers, and water channels, unlike isolated ships in open water, the asphalt grid of parked cars in parking lots, or single elevated roadways of bridges.
industrial_area: Characterized by clusters of large warehouses with flat roofs and adjacent paved lots, unlike the open vehicle grids of parking lots, the isolated cylindrical silos of storage tanks, or the prominent cooling towers of thermal power stations.
intersection: Shows a cross-shaped or T-shaped junction of roads at the same elevation, lacking the circular central island of roundabouts, the multi-level crossing of overpasses, or the bordered grid layout of parking lots.
island: Identified by a landmass completely surrounded by water with distinct coastlines, unlike the floating broken white sheets of sea ice, the narrow sandy strips of beaches, or the continuous water body of lakes.
lake: Displays a large, stationary body of water filling a basin with a distinct shoreline, unlike the mixed vegetation and shallow water of wetlands, the terrestrial landmass of islands, or the narrow flowing channels of rivers.
meadow: Characterized by natural, uneven green grassland without distinct crop rows or manicured boundaries, unlike the geometric plots of rectangular farmlands, the dense tree canopy of forests, or the sand traps and paths of golf courses.
medium_residential: Features a balanced layout of detached houses with visible yards and street grids, unlike the narrow uniform rectangles of mobile home parks, the tightly packed roofs of dense residential areas, or the isolated scattered homes of sparse residential areas.
mobile_home_park: Identified by closely spaced, narrow rectangular structures arranged in neat rows on small lots, unlike the larger varied houses of medium residential areas, the multi-story buildings of dense residential areas, or the diamond-shaped dirt infields of baseball fields.
mountain: Exhibits high topographic relief with steep slopes and rocky textures, unlike the bright snow-capped peaks of snowbergs, the flat barren expanses of deserts, or the geometric flat plots of rectangular farmlands.
overpass: Characterized by a multi-tiered road structure where one elevated road crosses over another, lacking the continuous length of freeways, the same-level crossing of intersections, or the water-spanning supports of bridges.
palace: Displays a large, sprawling historical building with symmetrical wings and courtyards, unlike the single steeples of churches, the modern rectangular blocks of commercial areas, or the small clustered homes of medium residential areas.
parking_lot: Shows a large, flat paved area with painted grid lines and distributed parked vehicles, unlike the large warehouses of industrial areas, the water-filled docks of harbors, or the long continuous concrete of runways.
railway: Identified by long, straight parallel steel rails on gravel beds, differing from the clustered platforms and buildings of railway stations, the paved multi-lane surfaces of freeways, or the elevated structures spanning water of bridges.
railway_station: Features a cluster of linear passenger platforms and station buildings adjacent to parallel tracks, unlike isolated railway lines, the storage warehouses of industrial areas, or the wide paved strips of runways.
rectangular_farmland: Displays geometric, straight-edged fields with varying crop colors, unlike the circular pivot-irrigated plots of circular farmlands, the stepped topography of terraces, or the natural uneven grass of meadows.
river: Characterized by a narrow, continuous, and winding channel of water cutting through land, unlike the landlocked masses of islands, the mixed marshy vegetation of wetlands, or the wide stationary basins of lakes.
roundabout: Shows a circular road junction with a central island, lacking the cross-shaped junctions of intersections, the multi-level elevation of overpasses, or the painted grid spaces of parking lots.
runway: Identified by a very long, wide, straight strip of dark asphalt with central white markings, distinct from the surrounding multiple buildings of an airport, the winged shape of an airplane, or the traffic lanes of a freeway.
sea_ice: Displays broken, floating sheets of white ice on the ocean surface, unlike the solid terrestrial landmass of islands, the peaked elevations of snowbergs, or the distinct hull shapes of ships.
ship: Features a distinct elongated hull shape with a pointed bow floating in open water, unlike the stationary piers and docks of harbors, the continuous ice sheets of sea ice, or the stationary landmass of islands.
snowberg: Characterized by bright white, peaked topography with steep glacial slopes, unlike the rocky and barren surfaces of mountains, the flat floating sheets of sea ice, or the amorphous drifting shapes of clouds.
sparse_residential: Features widely scattered individual houses separated by large areas of natural land or fields, unlike the continuous street grids of medium residential areas, the neat rows of mobile home parks, or the continuous geometric crop boundaries of rectangular farmlands.
stadium: Identified by a massive oval or circular enclosed structure with tiered seating surrounding a central field, unlike the small diamond shape of baseball fields, the open track and field areas, or the small rectangles of tennis courts.
storage_tank: Shows distinct cylindrical structures with domed or flat roofs and shadows indicating their height, unlike the flat-roofed warehouses of industrial areas, the cooling towers of thermal power stations, or the peaked roofs of churches.
tennis_court: Displays a rectangular surface with distinct net lines and boundary markings, unlike the circular hoops on basketball courts, the surrounding houses of medium residential areas, or the large warehouses of industrial areas.
terrace: Characterized by step-like agricultural fields carved into steep mountainsides, unlike the flat geometric plots of rectangular farmlands, the vertical walls of churches, or the manicured flat greens of golf courses.
thermal_power_station: Features large industrial buildings paired with distinct, massive hyperbolic cooling towers emitting white vapor, unlike the flat-roofed warehouses of industrial areas, the cylindrical storage tanks, or the natural amorphous shapes of clouds.
wetland: Displays a mixed spatial pattern of shallow water bodies interwoven with patches of marsh vegetation, unlike the continuous open water of lakes, the solid landmass of islands, or the narrow channel of rivers.
